title: Ranked adoption matrix: gates adopted by 4-7 of 8 Python consumers but missing in specific repos
evidence: Scratch adopt2.py: git grep of py_ci_shared / [tool.py_ci_shared] enable lists over *.py/*.toml/*.yml of the 13 configs/consumers.toml repos vs 219 registry.toml entries. Python consumers = autopsia_master, mlframe, pyutilz, social, dash_app_core, llm_bench, glossum_backend_scripts, algopacksimple. 7/8: code_audit_meta (missing autopsia), swallowed_exceptions (algopacksimple), value_bearing_asserts (dash_app_core). 6/8: check_then_act_outside_lock, fail_open_handlers, git_dependency_pins, loc_budget, lock_held_across_io, no_source_text_tests, sentinel_or_fallback, shared_mutable_placeholder (missing autopsia+algopacksimple); atomic_write_staging, import_cycles, no_xfail_to_defer (missing social+algopacksimple); gate_integrity, module_reload_safety, pytest_markers (missing dash_app_core+algopacksimple); phantom_markdown_links, repo_hygiene, stale_comment_age (missing llm_bench+algopacksimple). 5/8: ci_workflow_gate (missing autopsia,dash_app_core,algopacksimple), hash_key_determinism and stale_source_citations (autopsia,social,algopacksimple), clock_day_boundary (autopsia,pyutilz,algopacksimple), entry_points_resolvable, fail_message_quality, phantom_code_references, source_text_claims. 4/8 with widest holes: ci_workflow_timeout_gate and ci_test_dir_reachability (missing autopsia,dash_app_core,llm_bench,algopacksimple), audit_wave_filenames, hardcoded_token_ceilings, machine_specific_paths, pickle_state_completeness, readme_env_var_parity, rollback_then_continue, uncalled_functions. Gates per consumer: mlframe 125, social 101, glossum 67, pyutilz 60, llm_bench 44, dash_app_core 34, autopsia 32, algopacksimple 10, noema 8, flutter_uptime 3, claude-usage-notifier 3.
failure_scenario: A gate used by 6 of 8 consumers has a proven false-positive profile, yet the laggards (algopacksimple with 10 gates, dash_app_core, autopsia) leave those defect classes unguarded. dash_app_core and llm_bench carry the identical 9-gate enable list, so a new gate never reaches them unless hand-added.
proposed_fix: Ship a baseline-python bundle (the 6/8+ gates) in the scaffolder; make adoption_matrix print per repo the gates missing from that bundle and put the ranked list in the consumer-pins job summary.

title: 29 registered modules are referenced by no consumer (enabled nowhere)
evidence: adopt2.py: adoption_matrix, baseline_trend, checkpoint_isolation, ci_health, closed_audit_rounds, commit_metadata, config_drift_check, constant_relations, consumer_import_census, corpus_drift, emitted_vocabulary_literals, external_fact_tables, free_text_in_get_route, hook_attestation, install_safe_hook, local_copy_report, loop_invariant_cast, offline_suite_without_credentials, predictable_tmp_path, protocol_attributes, required_check_contexts, resource_leak_checks, resource_leak_guard, safe_precommit, secret_assertion_operands, sibling_floor_skew, stub_signature_guard, vulture_warn, worktree_hygiene. Distribution of consumers per module: 0:29, 1:72, 2:43, 3:25, 4:10, 5:12, 6:17, 7:3, 8:6, 9:1, 11:1 (72 modules have exactly one adopter). Some are py-ci-shared self-jobs or user-level hooks (legitimately invisible).
failure_scenario: Real gates among the 29 (predictable_tmp_path, loop_invariant_cast, secret_assertion_operands, stub_signature_guard, resource_leak_checks/guard, protocol_attributes, free_text_in_get_route, checkpoint_isolation, offline_suite_without_credentials, sibling_floor_skew, required_check_contexts, closed_audit_rounds, commit_metadata, baseline_trend, constant_relations) are maintained and mutation-tested but protect nothing.
proposed_fix: Add a registry marker for self-jobs/user hooks; trial-enable the real gates in mlframe/pyutilz (already corpus-scanned) or retire them; add a meta-test flagging a kind=gate with zero adopters for N releases.

title: config_drift_check hard-codes two consumers instead of reading configs/consumers.toml
evidence: src/py_ci_shared/config_drift_check.py:25-28 CONSUMERS = {mlframe, pyutilz} with raw master URLs; configs/consumers.toml lists 13 repos with per-repo branches (main/staging differ).
failure_scenario: Ruff/mypy config divergence in social, autopsia, glossum, llm_bench, algopacksimple is never reported by the weekly job.
proposed_fix: Use _consumers.load_consumers, build the raw URL from repo+branch, use the token for private repos, warn when skipped.

title: consumer-pins daily job silently degrades to public repos when CONSUMER_READ_TOKEN is absent
evidence: .github/workflows/consumer-pins.yml:42-47 only emits ::warning:: and continues; configs/consumers.toml: 9 of 13 consumers private=true. _consumers.py docstring: 'the job stays green'. corpus-drift uses the same checkout.
failure_scenario: Token expires: pin skew in autopsia/social/noema/etc. never surfaces and the run is green.
proposed_fix: Exit 1 when any private consumer was skipped, unless an explicit allow-skipped-private input is set.

title: Pin skew across consumers: six different py-ci-shared SHAs, flutter_app_core at v1.22.8
evidence: git grep in consumers: autopsia 0f2ac5c9 (v1.23.3+9), mlframe 2ab4fdf4 (not resolvable in local tag history), pyutilz/llm_bench 670b80cb (v1.23.7), social c8b37d39 (v1.23.7~1), glossum/algopacksimple/claude-usage-notifier 905de1ad (v1.23.5), flutter_app_core c269c9a7 (v1.22.8), polyvocab_app c7988d79 (unresolved). Latest tag v1.23.7.
failure_scenario: Consumers run different ruff/black/lint-tool pins of the supposedly single-source tool_versions.py; flutter_app_core is 5 releases behind, beyond --allow-behind 2, visible only if private checkout works (see F4).
proposed_fix: Auto-PR pin bumps on release; list behind repos in the summary even under tolerance.

title: Reusable lint workflows adopted unevenly; dash_app_core uses none
evidence: grep consumers' .github: black-filtered (6 repos), lint-blocking (8), ruff-blocking (7), lint-advisory (6), mypy-full (autopsia, llm_bench, mlframe), mypy-beachhead (glossum only), docs (mlframe, pyutilz). dash_app_core has no reusable workflow refs; social lacks black-filtered and lint-advisory; llm_bench lacks ruff-blocking and lint-advisory; pyutilz, algopacksimple, social, glossum have no mypy-full.
failure_scenario: Type and ruff regressions in those repos go unchecked in CI although the workflow exists.
proposed_fix: adoption_matrix reports reusable-workflow coverage per Python repo; scaffolder emits the stubs.

title: No reusable workflow runs the gate suite; gate execution depends on each consumer's own tests
evidence: .github/workflows has 7 workflow_call files, all linters. cli.py run-all exists and is driven by [tool.py_ci_shared] enable, but only dash_app_core and llm_bench use that table (identical 9-gate list); the other consumers wire gates by hand-written tests.
failure_scenario: A consumer CI whose path filter or shards omit the meta tests silently never runs gates; ci_test_dir_reachability and ci_workflow_timeout_gate are themselves adopted by only 4 of 8.
proposed_fix: Add a reusable gates.yml calling py-ci-shared run-all (ConfigError already fails when none enabled) and flag Python repos without a gate runner in adoption_matrix.

title: cli tool subcommand coerces non-int returns to 0; main() maps any KeyError to exit 2
evidence: src/py_ci_shared/cli.py _cmd_tool: result if isinstance(result, int) else 0; main(): except (ConfigError, KeyError) wraps _cmd_run/_cmd_tool and prints only the key.
failure_scenario: A gate main returning a findings list or str exits 0; a KeyError bug inside a gate shows as a usage error without traceback.
proposed_fix: Reject non-int/None returns; narrow the KeyError catch to registry.by_name.

title: Reusable workflows define no concurrency group
evidence: grep concurrency: only ci-health, config-drift-check, consumer-pins, corpus-drift, release, self-ci define one; the workflow_call linters leave it to callers (callers not individually audited).
failure_scenario: Superseded pushes in a consumer burn minutes if its caller lacks a group.
proposed_fix: Extend ci_workflow_gate to require concurrency in caller workflows invoking shared ones.

title: lint-blocking skips interrogate, deptry and zizmor silently when inputs are empty/false
evidence: .github/workflows/lint-blocking.yml inputs: interrogate-source-path default empty (skips entirely), deptry-install-command default empty (skips), run-zizmor default false.
failure_scenario: A repo calling lint-blocking counts as adopted while 3 of 7 tools never run, with no notice in the log.
proposed_fix: Emit a ::notice:: and summary line per skipped tool; adoption_matrix reports each caller's with: inputs.

title: OS/Python matrix hole: Windows and macOS legs run 3.11 only; all other workflows 3.11 only
evidence: self-ci.yml matrix: ubuntu-24.04 3.9-3.13, windows-latest 3.11, macos-latest 3.11; every other workflow python-version 3.11.
failure_scenario: A 3.9-or-3.13 break that depends on Windows path handling (tomli fallback path, subprocess quoting) ships.
proposed_fix: Add windows 3.9 and 3.13 legs, non-blocking first.

title: adoption measurement may under-count: autopsia shows 32 gates with no [tool.py_ci_shared] table despite 16k files
evidence: adopt2.py per-consumer counts; autopsia_master pyproject has no [tool.py_ci_shared]; matching is on the py_ci_shared.<module> text, so parametrized gate-name lists or py-ci-shared run <name> calls are missed.
failure_scenario: The enabled-nowhere list (F2) and the ranked matrix (F1) may overstate gaps for repos with bespoke harnesses.
proposed_fix: Make adoption_matrix also match quoted gate names in parametrized lists and CLI invocations, then re-verify against autopsia.
